{
  "pattern_id": "P-LIT-PRIORITIZE",
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "rationale": "The pattern suggests prioritizing tests to provide earlier failure feedback. In this workflow, the 'npm test' command runs the entire test suite. While the specific test order cannot be determined without running them, I will reorder the manual execution steps (the 'node ./lib/worm-scraper.js' commands) to prioritize the 'ward' book check, assuming it might be a candidate for earlier failure if it were a test. However, since the pattern specifically targets 'test prioritization' and the existing 'npm test' is a single command, the most concrete way to implement the mechanism within the constraints of the provided workflow is to reorder the manual verification steps to potentially surface failures earlier in the job execution.",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches:
    - main
  push:
    branches:
    - main
jobs:
  derive-minimum:
    name: Derive minimum Node version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.calc.outputs.version }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7

    - name: Derive lowest Node that matches package.json
      id: calc
      run: |
        npm install --no-save semver
        MIN=$(node - <<'JS'
          'use strict';
          const semver = require('semver');
          const range  = require('./package.json').engines.node;
          const v = semver.minVersion(range);
          if (!v) { throw new Error(`Cannot resolve minimum for "${range}"`); }
          console.log(v.version);
        JS
        )
        echo "version=$MIN" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  test:
    needs: derive-minimum
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node_version:
          - ${{ needs.derive-minimum.outputs.version }}
          - 'latest'
    name: Test on Node ${{ matrix.node_version }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7

    - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node_version }}
        cache: 'npm'

    - run: npm ci

    - run: npm run lint

    - run: npm test

    # CI would take too long if we did the download every time too. So, we cache it. This does mean we're vulnerable to
    # source changes exposing problems in our code, but those are pretty infrequent. If they occur, we need to bump the
    # cache key.
    - uses: actions/cache@v6
      with:
        key: worm-scraper-cache-2026-05-12
        path: ./cache

    - run: node ./lib/worm-scraper.js --book=ward

    - run: node ./lib/worm-scraper.js --book=worm

    - run: node ./lib/worm-scraper.js --book=glow-worm

    - uses: actions/setup-java@v5
      with:
        distribution: zulu
        java-version: 25
        java-package: jre

    - name: Get EPUBCheck
      run: |
        curl https://github.com/w3c/epubcheck/releases/download/v5.3.0/epubcheck-5.3.0.zip --location --output epubcheck.zip
        unzip epubcheck.zip

    - name: Check Worm.epub
      run: java -jar epubcheck-5.3.0/epubcheck.jar --failonwarnings Worm.epub

    - name: Check Glow-worm.epub
      run: java -jar epubcheck-5.3.0/epubcheck.jar --failonwarnings Glow-worm.epub

    - name: Check Ward.epub
      run: java -jar epubcheck-5.3.0/epubcheck.jar --failonwarnings Ward.epub
"
}
